My Second Bosch Dishwasher - My 15-year old Bosch SMU 4000 died, and the research on a popular consumer site said that the top 8 dishwashers were Bosch (including this model). I also trust the reviews on Amazon, and was surprised to see the low ratings of the Bosch dishwashers. So I looked around (in person) at the other brands available and just dreaded buying anything else but Bosch. Several of the Amazon reviews had a low rating because the capacity is lower than the piece of junk they just scrapped. It makes sense to me that to make these dishwashers quiet they probably need more insulation, and it's not possible to make the dishwasher larger on the outside, so they may sacrifice some space on the inside. I accept that trade-off gladly. I did not research to see if the smaller space claim was true, because I don't mind if I have more frequent smaller loads. I liked the layout after I used it a few times, and seems very similar to my old Bosch. And it is quiet - noticeably quieter than my old one.

The Bosch reviews in Amazon are so low and the consumer reviews are so high, that it makes me wonder who is writing the Amazon reviews. In this case only, I am glad that I didn't trust them.

Fits into LG LFXS30766S - My LG LFXS30766S refrigerator was icing up in the refrigerator compartment behind the bottom drawer. One symptom was that the drain hole iced over, so when the defrost the water could not get into the bottom evaporator pan and I would have pooled water in the refrigerator, where it would eventually freeze.

I initially solved the clogging issue with a short copper wire. I had some scraps of electrical wire that I stripped off the coating and wrapped it around the defrost line and had the wire extend down into the drain hole. A YouTube video shows how this works. The concept is the defrost line heats up and the heat extends to the copper wire in the drain hole. This copper wire trick worked.

While searching for a solution I came across these drain clips and I figured they would work even better due to the larger surface area. The next time I had to work on my refrigerator I pushed the copper wire aside and attached this clip. I had to bend the tip so the tip was not touching the plastic drain tube. These are made for a Samsung, but they work fine in an LG, and are easier to install than a copper wire because the clip right to the defrost line instead of having to be wrapped around with pliers. I bought two of these in case I have to install the same thing in the freezer compartment, or in case I need to solve this same problem in another refrigerator.

An earlier clog with similar symptoms was caused by hard water deposits clogging the bottom of the drain tube, where it touches the evaporator pan in the back. I fixed this by cutting off the bottom of the drain tube to leave a gap between the drain tube and the pan.

My refrigerator was still icing over after the copper wire fix, although the problem of water not draining was addressed. I am swapping a replacement defrost sensor next to see if that helps, which is why I had the back off to install this drain clip.

Efficient Means to Moisturized Air - One of my kids has issues with sinuses and if the air is too dry, she tends to wake up stuffy and with a dry throat. A humidifier is the key to solving this problem and so I turned to this humidifier from Vycol for the relief my daughter needed.

With this humidifier, you get digital accuracy and control. This is one of its best features. You can set it for the exact level of humidity you prefer. It will then keep the air at that level of humidity. It has a timer, too, which is good for my daughter. She can make sure it is off when she is not in the room.

Another thing I like about this humidifier is that you can visibly see the mist. With others I have used, the amount of moisture added to the air is too slight to visibly see it. With this humidifier, you can see the moisture shooting out from the top. And for a small bedroom, it adds moisture to the air quickly. You need to be careful not to set it too high for that reason. It adds humidity to a room rather quickly and it doesn’t make much noise.

A little moisture in the air is necessary for some people. This table top humidifier from Vycol certainly does its job, as promised. You can control it and set it the way you like. It adds moisture to a room quickly and efficiently and it looks better than other humidifiers. It earns an enthusiastic recommendation from me.

Use screws and attach firmly. This will prevent hoses from coming undone. I have horizontal sliding windows but height of window was greater than length of the pieces that fir in there so had to make an extension, but it is easy. Attach the bottom hose from the window to the intake side of the AC and the discharge should go to upper hole. Heat rises. This is my first portable ac, and if you need a portable, this isn't too bad and has dual hoses, so that is a plus. The unit is fairly noisy, but aren't they all. The fan..even on low, blows pretty hard, but cooling is good. Cooling won't be the same for each user, as more than likely room to be cooled might/might not be insulated, and therefore allows more heat to come in regardless. The ac unit does put out plenty of cool air. How your room absorbs it will depend on your room. Overall, at the price I paid, this is a good unit with dual hoses which is a plus. I wrapped the discharge hose loosely with tin foil and this prevents much heat from leaking from the hose walls into the room you are trying to cool. I do not think any of these portable units work quite as good as a window unit and these portable units are certainly take more space up in your room. Happy cooling. I will come back if there are issues, but so far, this unit works quite well.
